top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises targeted protein degradation as a new chemical modality: designed small molecules, whether bifunctional PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies) or cereblon-dependent glues (Handa), bring a chosen protein to an E3 ligase and convert occupancy-based pharmacology into event-driven degradation. The mechanism is chemically explicit and independently reproduced for two decades, and the cereblon strand is already clinically validated in myeloma. The allocation leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim, and no bifunctional degrader is approved yet, but a single citation naming the shared induced-proximity principle is honest enough, and the field has no earlier prize. P002 (Buchwald and Hartwig) is a clean, mature second choice with settled credit, but it is a later chapter of the cross-coupling field honoured in 2010. No award is worse than either.
